answer: Each agent must stake a refundable bond in a scarce token before voting, and every vote is weighted by how long that stake has been locked, not by how many wallets an operator runs. A Sybil farm pays the stake per identity yet earns only the weight of one freshly locked lane, so influence costs the stake times the identities needed, while an honest agent keeps its capital and loses only the time-value of locking it. Registering wallets opens no pearl: there is no cheap haven of instant voting power. The farm ends up on barren karst, spending far more than any honest rival for the same say.
